newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai feedmills to ask lifting of soymeal tariff.
newsitem.headline: Thai feedmills to ask lifting of soymeal tariff.

text.p: Thai animal feed producers will soon ask the government to remove 10 percent import tariff on soymeal, an industry source said on Sunday.
The source told Reuters that the cost of animal feed production has risen since late last year after a surge in soymeal prices and the tariff has added to the burden passed to consumers.

"Since the consumption of imported soymeal has risen sharply due to high demand in the feed industry, the government should consider removing the import tariff. We will make the request soon," said the source who is a member of Thai Feedmills Association.

The industry estimated that soymeal imports this year will reach one million tonnes compared with 828,337 tonnes last year. The domestic output of soybean for 1997/98 crop year (April-March) is expected to be around 383,623 tonnes, far below the demand in both oil crushing and animal feed production industry.
